header: Convoy counterflow  ·  take 1 of 3  ·  VLM: Gemini Robotics-ER 2
camera_label: Left: real overhead camera of the simulation (topic /perception/annotated_frame). The boxes and robot ids were drawn on it by the perception module (M1) during the run.
intro_lines: Two robots meet in a narrow gate between two barriers. Two more robots wait at the west end, held back at the start; their goals lie east of the gate. When a robot has been stuck for 12 s, the system asks a vision-language model (VLM) what to do: it sends a text prompt and the current camera image, checks the answer, and executes it.
This scenario uses the older ('legacy') grounding, which commands only the robots the model names.
Robots: 4  ·  Model: Gemini Robotics-ER 2 (gemini-robotics-er-2-preview)  ·  Take 1 of 3 (the selected take), recorded 2026-11-15.
Left: real overhead camera of the simulation. Right: the run's own logs, replayed in sync with simulation time.
watch_for: Which robots the model's first answer names (yellow lines on the right).
What happens to the two queued robots that it does not command.
What the check does with the later answers (orange lines).

captions.text: robot_1 and robot_2 drive toward each other into the gate; robot_3 and robot_4 wait at the west end.
Trigger: robot_2 has been stuck for 12 s. The system sends the model a text prompt and the current camera image; the wait for its answer plays in real time.
Model's plan: robot_2 yields (backs out and pulls aside), robot_1 crosses; the queued robot_3 and robot_4 'continue'.
Check: accepted unchanged (provenance=vlm_verbatim). The legacy grounding commands only the robots the model named: robot_2 and robot_1.
Dispatch: robot_2 is sent 'yield'; robot_1 waits, then is escorted through the gate.
robot_2 has pulled aside; robot_1 is escorted through. robot_3 and robot_4 were released by their own start timer and follow robot_1 through the gate (they were never commanded).
By about sim 75 s all four robots stand east of the gate; two pairs are closer than 0.45 m and the safety monitor holds them still. No robot moves again.
The model is asked again. From here on every proposal is refused by a grounding check or has no legacy template; each runs only as an 8 s wait.
Check: refused ('both robots outside the corridor on the same side'); the command becomes an 8 s wait.
This answer named all four robots, but the first-passer check refused it. It came about 190 s after the first trigger, with the four robots already held.

outcome.text: Outcome: Unresolved failure: 0 of 4 robots arrived by the end of the take (sim 260 s).

legend: Legend: yield = back out and pull aside · cross = drive through · continue = keep driving · temporary_wait = hold still · provenance: vlm_verbatim = plan accepted unchanged, repaired = edited by the verifier, m3_default = replaced by the grounding module's default plan · dispatch_order_source=chi = the system's own ordering · 'safety stop … min_distance_violation' (dim) = robots closer than 0.45 m are held still by the safety monitor.
disclosure: Illustrative demo, not controlled experimental evidence. Shown before the registered convoy experiment's VLM arm ran.
outro_title: Outcome: Unresolved failure  ·  take 1 of 3 (selected take)
outro_lines: 0 of 4 robots arrived. Takes 2 and 3 were also 0 of 4.
The model's: the first answer's yield (robot_2 backs out, robot_1 passes), executed as named. It left out the two queued robots.

The system's: when to ask; the legacy grounding, which commanded only the named pair; the start timer that released robot_3 and robot_4; the safety monitor holding the four robots once they were closer than 0.45 m; the later proposals: all 11 ran as 8 s waits (10 refused by grounding checks, 1 had no legacy template).
